searchText: From eip-2929: > In particular, if a scope reverts, the access lists should be in the state they were in before that scope was entered. This seems like a bad design because I can pay to access the same slot multiple times if the first access happens during an internal revert. Internal reverts are good to run on-chain simulations because you can pretend to do something and return information about the new state in the revert data. Is it really a cache miss again after revert? I think the intent is that side effects of revert are unobserbable, hence rolling back the warm state The warm state is only observable via the gas opcode and out-of-gas but I guess that counts It falls into the same bucket as reverting empty touches too so it's consistently annoying The cost of warming storage is 2000 if you do it in SLOAD (100 vs 2100) but it's +2100 if you do it in SSTORE. that's pretty annoying dumb eip What is the maximum depth of the container? I mean how many times Container can refer to sub-container and that to another sub-container and so on? until it fills 48k bytes. Maximum subcontainers should be one of our reference test items for sure. I meant if in case `CREATE3 -> CREATE3 -> CREATE3 -> and so on` how many calls it can do? 1024 is the call stack limit so the lesser of those two thanks! in practice I can only reach a depth of 0x1c8 for 30m gas due to the L function 1/64th rule strikes again.

From eip-2929:
> In particular, if a scope reverts, the access lists should be in the state they were in before that scope was entered.
This seems like a bad design because I can pay to access the same slot multiple times if the first access happens during an internal revert.
